title: Eco-Industrial Park (EIP)
subtitle: A Connected Industrial Ecosystem for Large-Scale Waste Recovery and Circular Resource Management
category: Sustainable Infrastructure & Industrial Systems Startup Project
shortDescription: Eco-Industrial Park (EIP) is an under-development industrial infrastructure concept designed to bring multiple recycling industries together within one connected ecosystem, with a focus on maximum resource recovery, shared infrastructure, circular material flow, reduced environmental impact, and long-term resource security.
fullDescription: Eco-Industrial Park (EIP) is an ongoing research and startup-oriented project exploring a large-scale integrated approach to waste management and resource recovery. Instead of treating different waste streams as completely separate industries, EIP envisions a connected industrial ecosystem where multiple recycling and recovery sectors can operate together and support one another. The broader concept covers e-waste, plastics, metals, paper, glass, rubber and tyres, batteries, organic waste, construction and demolition waste, medical waste, oil and chemical waste, water recovery, waste-to-energy, and future recycling sectors. The project focuses on how shared infrastructure, interconnected industries, resource recovery, renewable energy, water management, and coordinated industrial planning could create a more efficient recycling ecosystem. A major project component is the development of an automatic PCB dismantling concept as part of the e-waste segment. EIP is currently in the research and development stage, with the overall objective of studying existing recycling systems, comparing different approaches, identifying practical limitations, and developing a scalable model suited to Indian conditions. The long-term vision is to create an integrated industrial platform that can recover greater value from waste, support domestic raw-material availability, reduce environmental impact, and contribute to a stronger circular economy.
problemStatement: Waste management and recycling are often divided among separate industries, facilities, processes, and supply chains. This can create fragmented material flows, duplicated infrastructure, transportation requirements, inconsistent recovery outcomes, and loss of potentially valuable resources. Different waste categories also require different processing capabilities, making large-scale resource recovery a complex industrial challenge. EIP explores whether these individual systems can be planned as a connected industrial ecosystem rather than as isolated recycling facilities. The project therefore focuses on the broader challenge of creating an infrastructure model that can accommodate diverse waste streams while improving resource utilization, industrial connectivity, recovery potential, and long-term sustainability.
solution: EIP proposes an integrated industrial ecosystem in which multiple recycling and resource-recovery sectors are planned as interconnected facilities within a common industrial environment. The concept combines centralized infrastructure, shared utilities, coordinated material movement, resource recovery, renewable energy integration, water management, and multiple specialized recycling sectors. The objective is to create an ecosystem where different industries can complement one another instead of operating independently. The project also considers reusable components, recovered materials, secondary raw materials, and other useful outputs as potential resources within the wider industrial network. Rather than focusing on a single waste category, EIP is being developed as a scalable platform capable of expanding across multiple waste streams and future recycling technologies.
